s: is_ruled_by King Bud Noland is a kingdom ruled by King Bud. Kiki Aru rests there overnight, receives supper and a bed from a family, and leaves after breakfast.

l: Land of Ev, The Magic of Oz
s: uses money [for payment of food and lodging] The Land of Ev requires people to pay money for food and lodging at an inn. Kiki Aru travels through the land on foot, steals a gold piece there, and then continues on his way.

l: gold piece (old man), The Magic of Oz
s: belongs_to old man (Ev inn) [as part of his heap of gold] An old man in the Land of Ev is counting a heap of gold pieces when Kiki Aru takes one through an open window in the form of a magpie. Kiki later resumes his own shape and puts the gold piece in his pocket.
A sparrow watches Kiki Aru steal a gold piece and transform, condemns magic as wicked and unlawful, warns of future regret, then flies away.

l: Kiki's theft of the gold piece, The Magic of Oz
s: is_a crime [a greater crime than magic, according to the sparrow] Kiki Aru commits the theft of a gold piece by transforming into a magpie and taking it from an old man's pile. The sparrow witnesses the theft and calls it a crime.

is_used_for food and lodging [in the Land of Ev] In the Land of Ev, money is needed to obtain food and lodging. Kiki Aru has none, so he takes a gold piece; in the Land of Oz, people do not use money and may take what they want without price.

Ruggedo is a cruel, crafty, immortal Nome and former Nome King. After pressure from the Oz people, he abdicates or is expelled from the Kingdom of the Nomes, loses his kingdom and magic tools, and wanders with many pockets stuffed with diamonds, rubies, and emeralds. He fears eggs, which he considers dangerous. His central purpose is revenge: he wants to conquer Oz, punish Ozma, Dorothy, the Wizard, Glinda, and other Oz people, and regain his former power and kingdom. He joins Kiki Aru, offering him rule as King of Oz while secretly intending to learn Kiki's magic word, transform Kiki into faggots, and burn him. Transformed into an eagle, he enters the Forest of Gugu with Kiki to recruit beasts. He helps create a composite beast form with lions' heads, monkeys' bodies, and wild-asses' tails, takes the invented identity of a Li-Mon-Eag, and deceives the beasts by claiming Oz plans to enslave them. He urges them to conquer Oz and proposes turning beasts into people and Oz people into beasts. While concealed as a beast, Ruggedo recognizes the Wizard, Dorothy, the Cowardly Lion, and the Hungry Tiger as dangerous enemies. Kiki transforms him into a goose; ashamed and frightened, Ruggedo hides his identity and searches for the Wizard's black bag, still hoping to use Kiki's transformations against Oz. Kiki restores him to the Li-Mon-Eag shape, but the Wizard learns the magic word and changes Ruggedo into an ordinary walnut. Restored to his natural Nome King form, Ruggedo again threatens conquest until he drinks the Water of Oblivion. He then forgets his identity, revenge, and knowledge, becomes harmless and innocent, and lives peacefully and happily in the Land of Oz.

l: the Scarecrow of Oz, The Magic of Oz
s: The Scarecrow of Oz is a happy-natured, witty straw-stuffed person, filled with straw in his legs, who prepares straw slippers for Ozma and entertains guests beside her at her birthday banquet.

l: the Tin Woodman, The Magic of Oz
s: The Tin Woodman, Emperor of the Winkie Country, prepares a girdle for Ozma’s birthday and attends her banquet with a brightly polished metal body, sitting beside her and entertaining guests without eating.

Dorothy is a fearless Kansas girl and a Princess of Oz, though she prefers simply to be called Dorothy and does not like the princess title. Ozma of Oz's dearest friend, she lives in luxurious rooms in the Royal Palace, frequently discovers hidden places in Oz, and is an old friend of the Wizard of Oz as well as a friend and companion of Trot and Cap'n Bill. Her story centers on loyalty, practical courage, and her wish to give Ozma a birthday gift. Worried that Ozma already has everything, she consults friends, seeks the Magic Flower, and joins the Wizard in obtaining and training twelve tiny dancing monkeys for a surprise cake they will give together. During these efforts, Dorothy defends the Cowardly Lion's courage, but Kiki transforms her into a lamb. She dislikes the form and wants to be as she was born; the Wizard restores her natural shape. She then helps search for his black bag, rescue giant soldiers, and travel with the Wizard, the Glass Cat, and caged monkeys. Riding the Cowardly Lion, she heads toward the Magic Isle to save Trot and Cap'n Bill. Alarmed that the captives may shrink away, she proposes seeking Glinda when needed and later suggests turning them into bumblebees, which helps them survive. Dorothy supports retrieving the Magic Flower, rides the Hungry Tiger with Trot while carrying the monkeys' cage, and cares for the injured Glass Cat by washing its eyes and ears. After the flower reaches the Royal Palace, she attends Ozma's feast beside the Scarecrow, presents the Surprise Cake, and delights in the monkeys' performance. At the end, she proposes using the Fountain of the Water of Oblivion so the transformed magicians forget their magic, helps Kiki Aru and Ruggedo drink it, and kindly seats the memoryless Kiki beside her.

l: the Oz people, The Magic of Oz
s: The Oz people are a people of the Land of Oz who live in Oz. They are generally happy, contented, and prosperous, love Ozma of Oz as their beautiful girl Ruler, and mix work and play so that both are delightful and satisfying. They took Ruggedo’s underground kingdom and magic tools, making him regard them as enemies. Ruggedo then falsely tells the forest animals that the Oz people intend to enslave them, urging conquest and transformation of the people into beasts. Some animals consider fighting, but representatives of the Oz side arrive as war threatens.

l: beasts of Oz, The Magic of Oz
s: The beasts of Oz live in its forests, do not die, and follow laws they made to restrain fighting, though conflicts still occur. Some savage beasts in remote places may follow a leader. Ruggedo seeks to recruit them as an army by promising transformation into men and women. In Gugu Forest, the animals argue over fighting the Oz people, transformation, or inaction; after Kiki's transformations, they panic and flee.

l: Emerald City, The Magic of Oz
s: Emerald City is the green capital at the center of Oz and of Ozma's dominions. Ozma's palace, also called the Royal Palace, stands at its center; the city has a vast garden, and its people visit Ozma's gardens and palace. It is homeward or a destination for several travelers: Dorothy returns from Glinda's Castle, plans a birthday present there, and visits the Wizard in his tower room. After the Wizard and Dorothy are transformed, they plan to return to seek Glinda the Good's help, while the Glass Cat leaves after learning the Wizard has gone to the Great Forest of Gugu. The Wizard later intends to bring twelve monkeys and keep them in his room until after Ozma's birthday; the party travels there, and the Glass Cat reaches the Royal Palace after escaping blue mud. Ozma hears Professor H. M. Wogglebug, T.E.'s appeal there, and the city prepares her birthday celebration.

l: Kingdom of the Nomes, The Magic of Oz
s: Ruggedo used to rule the Kingdom of the Nomes but was forced to abdicate and leave it. He hopes to regain it after obtaining enough magic through his plans in Oz.

l: Gillikin Country, The Magic of Oz
s: is_entered_after Munchkin Country [during the journey] The Gillikin Country has wild forests containing many monkeys. Dorothy and the Wizard plan to travel there to obtain monkeys for the surprise cake.

l: the transformations, The Magic of Oz
s: These are magical transformations, a kind of enchantment that changes a target’s form. They require a Magic Word or secret word spoken properly; a transformed human form that cannot speak it cannot change back, so becoming a tree would be permanent. Kiki Aru performs the transformations one at a time and can change himself and others into birds, beasts, dragons, fishes, and other beings that can talk in Oz, without the tools, passes, and many mystic words Ruggedo once needed. He first changes himself and Ruggedo into eagles, then into Li-Mon-Eags while keeping the word secret, and proves the power by turning Loo the Unicorn into a Gillikin man and back. During the proposed conquest, Kiki changes the Wizard, Dorothy, the Cowardly Lion, the Hungry Tiger, Gugu, and Ruggedo into different forms, leaving them confused and seeking the black bag for reversal. Finally, the Magic Word restores the Wizard, Dorothy, and the others; it also changes Ruggedo, monkeys, and Kiki into further forms.

l: conquest of Oz, The Magic of Oz
s: The conquest of Oz is Ruggedo's proposed and forest beasts' planned campaign to overthrow the people of Oz. Urging Kiki Aru, Ruggedo plans to enter Oz as birds, transform into powerful beasts, and recruit consenting savage beasts from Gugu Forest. Beasts that join are to be rewarded by transformation into humans, while Oz people are to be turned into beasts. The campaign would use a giant army: Kiki Aru is to transform fifty monkeys into uniformed giants with sharp swords to capture or destroy the people and make them slaves. The plan is interrupted when the Wizard learns the Magic Word.

l: Ruggedo's transformation plan, The Magic of Oz
s: Ruggedo's transformation plan is a revenge scheme against the Oz people who took his kingdom. He plans to turn the beasts of the Forest of Gugu into men and women and Oz people into beasts, then have the transformed beasts march into and conquer Oz, overcome or destroy its leaders, and use the resulting magic to recover his kingdom.

l: Ruggedo's jewels, The Magic of Oz
s: Ruggedo carries diamonds, rubies, and emeralds in specially made pockets. He uses the jewels to pay for the inn and offers them to Kiki in exchange for the secret of transformations.

l: Book of Records, The Magic of Oz
s: Glinda's Book of Records instantly records everything people do in the Land of Oz, but not beasts' actions; Ruggedo plans animal forms to avoid discovery.

l: animal transformations of the Oz people, The Magic of Oz
s: Ruggedo plans, after conquering Oz, to transform all its people into various beasts and send them to forests and jungles. In the proposed exchange, beasts become men and women with comforts, while the transformed Oz people must hunt and fight for food.

l: beasts' transformation into humans, The Magic of Oz
s: transforms beasts of Oz [into men and women] Ruggedo plans to promise the beasts of Oz that they will be transformed into men and women if they help conquer the country. They would then live in houses and enjoy the other good things available to people.

Oz is a fairyland and fine country, separated from the world by the Desert and ruled by Ozma. It protects guests from danger from outside lands. Its people and beasts do not die or become sick, though they can be destroyed. Oz contains the Winkie, Gillikin, Munchkin, and Quadling Countries and the Emerald City, and is home to the Cowardly Lion, the Wizard, Dorothy's companions, and the Hungry Tiger. Kiki Aru and Ruggedo plan to conquer Oz by turning forest beasts against its people, though Gugu says Oz has not been their enemy. While its people celebrate Ozma's birthday, Ozma and the Wizard keep Ruggedo in Oz to prevent his return to evil ways.

l: the conspiracy to conquer and rule Oz, The Magic of Oz
s: A conspiracy by Kiki Aru and Ruggedo to conquer and rule Oz begins with mutual distrust and deception. When Kiki fears the Wizard and Oz people will defeat it, Ruggedo forces his own approach while Kiki independently protects the plot.

l: Royal Palace, The Magic of Oz
s: Royal Palace is Ozma's royal residence at the center of an extensive, delightful garden in Emerald City, described as the most splendid building ever constructed. It contains the Throne Room where Ozma holds high court, luxurious rooms for Dorothy, a tower room for the Wizard of Oz, and marble stables for the Cowardly Lion and Hungry Tiger. Its open grounds include gardens and many features, and it hosts Ozma's birthday feast, with her animal friends seated at their own table.

Trot is a little girl, Ozma's guest and friend, and Cap'n Bill's oldest, most faithful comrade. Living at the Royal Palace, she joins Dorothy and Cap'n Bill in seeking the Magic Flower as Ozma's birthday gift, carrying a basket of food and traveling with Cap'n Bill under the Glass Cat's guidance. On the way she is frightened by forest sounds and a Kalidah, but follows Cap'n Bill across a river. Reaching the flower's island, she and Cap'n Bill are trapped when roots grow from their feet into the ground. Hungry, tired, and unable to move, Trot fears they may starve. She uses the flower to wish for fruit and eats it, but cannot wish herself free because the wishes affect only the plant. She befriends and advises the Lonesome Duck, who makes her a toadstool seat. While rescue is sought, she remains rooted, begins shrinking with Cap'n Bill, and explains that removing the flesh roots would hurt like cutting off fingers or toes. Dorothy and the others finally save them by changing Trot and Cap'n Bill into bumblebees; they return safely and regain their normal forms. Trot is delighted that the Magic Flower can still be Ozma's present, praises the Glass Cat's help, protects the flower during the journey home, keeps and waters it in her room, and lets only Betsy Bobbin and Dorothy see its blossoms. At Ozma's birthday feast, seated beside Cap'n Bill and opposite the Tin Woodman, she tells Ozma how the flower was obtained.

l: Cap'n Bill, The Magic of Oz
s: Cap'n Bill is an old, fat sailor-man with one wooden leg and one flesh leg, strong hands, a knife, and a stout cord. He is Trot's oldest and most faithful comrade and friend. Seeking the Magic Flower as a birthday present for Ozma, he joins Trot and the Glass Cat on the journey to the Magic Isle. On the way, he makes Trot a small shelter, protects her from a Kalidah, knocks the attacker down with his wooden leg, and pins it with a stake. He builds a raft from logs and stakes and propels Trot and the Glass Cat across the river. On the island, his flesh foot grows roots into the ground, leaving only his wooden leg free; Trot is rooted too. He recognizes that the Glass Cat must seek the Wizard of Oz's help. While trapped, Cap'n Bill waits beside Trot, eats fruit produced by the Magic Flower, reflects on ordinary blessings such as walking and breathing, and helps question the Lonesome Duck. Though seated on a strong toadstool, he remains unable to leave. He calls their condition being anchored and fears cutting or pulling up their flesh roots would hurt terribly. As he and Trot shrink to about half their natural size, he believes escape is hopeless and asks that Ozma be told if they are destroyed. Cap'n Bill is transformed into a bumblebee, escapes the Magic Isle safely, and is restored to his usual form. After binding bark to his good foot, he returns, retrieves the golden flower-pot containing the Magic Flower, and carries it away from the enchanted Isle. He later helps with a board for the Cowardly Lion, repairs the monkeys' cage wires, secretly brings the flower-pot to Trot's room, and attends Ozma's birthday feast beside Trot, credited with carrying the flower from the Isle.

l: Ozma's birthday, The Magic of Oz
s: Ozma's birthday is a great occasion celebrated throughout the Land of Oz with feasting, rejoicing, decorations, processions, games, plays, and other festivities. It begins with Dorothy, Trot, and Cap'n Bill planning a present, including the Magic Flower, though Ozma has everything she needs. The Wizard trains twelve tiny monkeys, shrinks and hides them in a cake. At the Royal Palace's grand feast, they emerge when Ozma cuts the cake, perform tricks, and are returned to the forest the next day.

l: Magic Flower, The Magic of Oz
s: Magic Flower is a curious, beautiful magic plant and flower that grows in a large, heavy golden flower-pot. It begins on a small island in a river running through a forest in the northern Munchkin Country, on the Magic Isle. Continuously, day and night, it changes from one kind of blossom to another, showing strikingly bright, glowing colors, unusual shapes, and successive varieties including peonies, lilies, chrysanthemums, daffodils, tulips, gladioli, yellow roses, and violets. Its flowers alternate with fruit: when Trot wishes for fruit, it produces many kinds for only a while; picked fruit remains good, but fruit left on the plant disappears, and the plant returns to flowers. Trot, Cap'n Bill, and the Glass Cat seek it as Ozma's birthday present, but their effort brings them into the magic of the queer island. Cap'n Bill eventually retrieves it. Because the pot is too heavy to carry, it is transported on a fitted board tied to the Cowardly Lion's back. Moved to Trot's room in the Royal Palace, it keeps its magic. At Ozma's birthday banquet it produces fragrant mammoth blossoms, fills the room with delicate fragrance, and is given to Ozma, who plans to place it in her boudoir.

l: the Glass Cat, The Magic of Oz
s: The Glass Cat is a magical, transparent crystal tabby made entirely of glass by Dr. Pipt before Ozma forbade magic; it is also described as made by a careless magician. Its body includes delicate pink jewel-like brains, a cold, hard ruby heart, large emerald eyes, a beautiful spun-glass tail, sharp glass claws and teeth, and glass feet. When clean, its moving brains and heart can be seen through its crystal body. It has no stomach or machinery for eating, so it neither eats mice nor feels hunger or thirst, despite having been made to catch mice. Tireless, free to move on the Magic Isle, and able to walk under a river, it is vain about its appearance and readily persuaded by praise. It knows Oz, including every path in the Great Forest of Gugu, hidden places, and the remote Munchkin Country location of the Magic Flower. It has visited the Isle of the Magic Flower, seen the flower bloom, and identifies its gold flower-pot. It tells Dorothy, Trot, and Cap'n Bill where the flower is hidden and guides Trot and Cap'n Bill to the island. After roots trap them there, Trot's promise to praise it as a hero persuades the Glass Cat to walk along the river bottom and seek the Wizard of Oz. Though it does not want Trot and Cap'n Bill to know it is sorry, it is troubled by having led them to the island. It travels to the Great Forest of Gugu, learns that the Wizard and Dorothy have been transformed, and helps search for the black bag and the Goose. It climbs an avocado tree, finds the black bag among leaves within five minutes, hides it, and leads the Wizard to it, demonstrating that its pink brains are effective hunters. It then guides travelers toward the river and reaches Trot and Cap'n Bill under the water, helping bring the Wizard to save them. Later, it teases monkeys by pulling their tails. They cover it in dark blue mud, making it dull blue and unable to see or hear until Dorothy cleans its eyes and ears. It washes in a nearby lake and is later found at the Royal Palace pretending not to notice the travelers. It is friends with Trot and Cap'n Bill despite its disagreeable ways and rivals the Pink Kitten over flesh and glass.

l: the river, The Magic of Oz
s: The river begins narrow and gradually broadens northward until it is as wide as a small lake around the tiny Isle of the Magic Flower at its center. After crossing the forest, travelers follow it upstream to the Magic Isle, where the river separates them from Trot and Cap'n Bill; only the Glass Cat can cross underwater.

l: the Magic Isle, The Magic of Oz
s: The Magic Isle, also called the Isle of the Magic Flower, is a tiny enchanted island in the middle of a river in the Gillikin Country of the Land of Oz, no more than fifty feet across. It is bare, with no trees, shrubs, grass, weeds, stones, or other growth; its only plant is the Magic Plant in a golden flower-pot at its center. Kalidahs avoid it because of its magic. The island’s chief danger is its enchantment: the Magic Flower lures strangers onto it, then flesh roots grow from living visitors’ feet into the ground, holding them unable to move or lift a foot. Those trapped also shrink day by day until nothing remains. Trot and Cap’n Bill arrive, become rooted prisoners, and begin shrinking. The flower can respond to wishes of people on the island, but it is also described as a trap meant to catch and destroy them. In the end, Cap’n Bill protects his foot with wood and carries the Magic Flower away.

l: Golden Flower-pot, The Magic of Oz
s: The golden flower-pot holds the Magic Flower on the Magic Isle. Trot and Cap'n Bill admire it but are trapped before moving it; later Cap'n Bill lifts it, carries it to the raft, and brings it to the riverbank.

l: Glass Cat's journey to the Magic Flower, The Magic of Oz
s: The Glass Cat's journey to the Magic Flower is a planned week-long trip with Trot and Cap'n Bill, guided by the Glass Cat to a hidden island by a river, reached by walking along its bottom because it cannot swim.

l: the Patchwork Girl, The Magic of Oz
s: Scraps is the strange Patchwork Girl, stuffed with cotton yet possessing mixed brains. She calls herself Scraps and, for Ozma's birthday, plans and writes a song whose unusually long title she considers stylish.

l: Wooden Sawhorse, The Magic of Oz
s: The Wooden Sawhorse is a living wooden creature of Oz: a small log body, knot eyes, tree-limb legs, and gold plates protecting its feet. Attached to Ozma, it is a swift, willing traveler; Dorothy rides with it in the Red Wagon, but the Wizard keeps it from the thick forests.

l: the Cowardly Lion, The Magic of Oz
s: The Cowardly Lion is a great, powerful lion, King of all Beasts, and a friendly champion who is Dorothy’s trusted companion and protects Dorothy and the Wizard of Oz. Though fearful and called cowardly, he is not simply a coward: when forced to fight he is a terrible fighter, yet he volunteers for danger and acts strongly. He lives in the Emerald City with the Hungry Tiger. As Gugu’s guest, he says he has not come to rule the forest, but Kiki transforms him into a little Munchkin boy. He helps seek the lost black bag and urges finding the Magician. He warns the others about the Magic Isle, then fears it but retrieves the raft by swimming there. He later carries the Magic Flower on a board fastened to his back.

l: the Hungry Tiger, The Magic of Oz
s: The Hungry Tiger is a monstrous, powerful but friendly champion who lives in the Emerald City with the Cowardly Lion and protects Dorothy and the Wizard of Oz. Always hungry for fat babies, he does not eat them because of his tender conscience. During the journey he carries the Wizard of Oz, a golden cage, and Dorothy and Trot. He eats a bee when the bees are the only food available, unaware that Trot and Cap'n Bill had become bees. After recognizing Kiki as responsible for transformations, he attacks him and is transformed into a Rabbit. He then stays with the transformed companions while they seek the Wizard's black bag and later bends cage bars while striking at the Glass Cat.

l: Red Wagon, The Magic of Oz
s: is_harnessed_to Wooden Sawhorse The Red Wagon is the royal wagon that Dorothy uses with the Wooden Sawhorse to travel to Glinda's Castle and back. The Wizard decides it cannot pass through the thick forests where the monkeys live.

l: Dorothy and the Wizard's Surprise Cake, The Magic of Oz
s: Dorothy and the Wizard's Surprise Cake is a huge frosted birthday cake for Ozma, decorated with candy flowers, candles, and an inscription. Dorothy plans its hollow, frosting-covered center to hide twelve tiny monkeys. When Ozma cuts the cake, the monkeys and their golden band instruments emerge to dance and give cake pieces to guests.

l: monkeys for the surprise cake, The Magic of Oz
s: Large wild monkeys from the Gillikin Country are to be shrunk to three inches, trained to dance and distribute cake, then hidden in Ozma's birthday cake until it is placed on the banquet table.

l: Ozma's birthday gifts, The Magic of Oz
s: Ozma's birthday gifts are a varied collection planned by her friends, including a Magic Flower, an emerald-thread gown, a song, a tin-and-emerald girdle, straw slippers, and a surprise cake. At the birthday party, they are placed on a Banquet Hall table; Ozma examines them and thanks the donors.

l: Ozma's birthday feast, The Magic of Oz
s: Ozma's customary grand birthday feast is planned in her palace's royal Banquet Hall for friends and animal companions. Ozma gives it; guests dine at a long table, animals at a smaller one, and gifts are displayed separately.

l: journey to find monkeys, The Magic of Oz
s: is_to wild forests of Gillikin Country [to search for wild monkeys] Dorothy and the Wizard plan a secret journey to the wild forests of the Gillikin Country to find monkeys for Ozma's surprise cake. They decide to travel with the Cowardly Lion and the Hungry Tiger because the Red Wagon cannot pass through the forests and the two animals can protect them from danger.

l: Forest of Gugu, The Magic of Oz
s: The Forest of Gugu, also called Gugu Forest and the Great Forest of Gugu, is a vast, great tangle of trees and the largest forest in Oz. It is described as being in the central western Gillikin Country and in the Munchkin Country, with rugged mountains adjoining its east side. Named for and ruled by Gugu the Leopard King under the Laws of the Forest, it houses many kinds of beasts, including most of Oz's wild and biggest beasts. Its clearing hosts important councils and monkey sentinels watch its edge. Ruggedo and Kiki Aru enter seeking support; troublemakers violate the Laws, leading Gugu to call a council. Later Kiki transforms several visitors and Gugu, while the Glass Cat follows the forest's paths. The Wizard and Dorothy are thereafter welcomed as friends of the beasts.

l: Gugu the Leopard, The Magic of Oz
s: Gugu the Leopard is an enormous yellow leopard and King of Gugu Forest, also called the Forest of Gugu. Advised by three King's Counselors, he leads the Council of Beasts, maintains laws and order, punishes beasts that start fights with the Counselors, and rules wisely, justly, and well. When Ruggedo claims that the people of Oz mean to enslave the beasts, Gugu initially doubts him. After Kiki Aru transforms Loo into a man, Gugu recognizes the strangers' magic, summons the beasts, presents the claimed danger, and urges careful deliberation over whether to fight. He welcomes the Cowardly Lion and companions as guests, but when he attacks Kiki, Kiki transforms him into a fat Gillikin woman. Indignant at this imposed form, Gugu is to be taken to Glinda the Good for restoration.

l: King's Counselors, The Magic of Oz
s: King's Counselors are Gugu's intelligent counselors: Bru the Bear, Loo the Unicorn, and Rango the Gray Ape. They hold office to advise Gugu on keeping laws and maintaining order among beasts.

l: Bru the Bear, The Magic of Oz
s: Bru the Bear, Counselor of Gugu the Leopard, challenges the Mixed Beast's warning and conquest proposal, valuing life as a Bear because he knows Bear ways.

l: Loo the Unicorn, The Magic of Oz
s: Loo the Unicorn, Counselor of Gugu the Leopard, angrily urges beasts to fight Oz’s people, becomes a man through Kiki Aru, enjoys it, and returns to unicorn form for safety.

l: Council of Beasts, The Magic of Oz
s: Council of Beasts, comprising Gugu the Leopard King, Bru the Bear, Rango the Gray Ape, and Loo the Unicorn, hears Ruggedo’s warning and proposal, questions his claims, and considers fighting the people of Oz.

l: Rango the Gray Ape, The Magic of Oz
s: Rango the Gray Ape is a wise, experienced gray ape, counselor to Gugu the Leopard, and chief of all the forest’s monkey tribes. He rejects the Li-Mon-Eags as mischief-makers, summons the forest beasts, recognizes a magician’s transformations, and seeks rescue for six monkeys. Though initially refusing to lend monkeys for Ozma’s birthday, he consents after assurances of their safe return.
Li-Mon-Eags are Ruggedo and Kiki Aru’s invented mixed-beast identities: Sky Island magicians who claim friendship with beasts, then deceptively warn them about the people of Oz.

l: beasts of the Forest of Gugu, The Magic of Oz
s: The beasts of the Forest of Gugu live under Gugu the Leopard’s leadership, obey its laws, and include monkey tribes. Warned by Ruggedo that Oz’s people may enslave them, they assemble in the Great Clearing, angrily consider fighting, but divide over his proposed transformation plan.

l: Great Clearing, The Magic of Oz
s: Great Clearing is a clearing in the Forest of Gugu where the Wizard restored enchanted beings; Rango comes to tell Gugu the King what happened, seek the Wizard’s help, and negotiate rescue of giant soldiers.

l: war between the beasts and the people of Oz, The Magic of Oz
s: The war between the beasts and the people of Oz is an alleged conflict said by Ruggedo to be planned by Oz. He uses the claim to urge the Council of Beasts to attack, but Gugu disputes any cause for war, and no decision is reached before Kiki interrupts the animals' debate.

l: enslavement of the forest beasts, The Magic of Oz
s: Enslavement of the forest beasts is Ruggedo's claimed plan that the people of Oz, including Ozma, will invade the Forest of Gugu, use ropes to capture and beat its beasts, and make them beasts of burden. He presents this threat to urge the beasts to conquer Oz first.

Kalidah is a creature whose especial home is the forest containing the Isle of the Magic Flower and which attacks other beasts ferociously. It approaches Trot and Cap'n Bill and attacks them, but Cap'n Bill pins it with a stake. It frees itself by forcing the stake through its body, leaving two holes; its anger fades, and it seeks the Kalidah King for healing.

l: the Kalidahs, The Magic of Oz
s: Kalidahs are the most disagreeable, powerful, and ferocious creatures in the Land of Oz. Living in a forest, they swim like ducks, attack other animals, often fight among themselves, and avoid the Isle of the Magic Flower because they dislike magic.

l: forest (the forest containing the Isle of the Magic Flower), The Magic of Oz
s: A forest beyond the settled parts of the Munchkin Country, with few or no houses or paths. It is the especial home of Kalidahs and also contains monkeys, few other beasts, and the Magic Isle across a river. As travelers cross into the Gillikin Country, its blue-green leaves turn purple.

l: the raft, The Magic of Oz
s: The raft is a small log raft built by Cap'n Bill with sharp-ended stakes to cross the river to the Isle of the Magic Flower, since he and Trot cannot travel beneath the water. Equipped with a long pole and a flat paddle he makes, it carries Trot, Cap'n Bill, and the Glass Cat to the Magic Isle. Left on its beach, it is later brought across the river by the Cowardly Lion and used by the Wizard to carry himself and Dorothy to the island.

l: the magic of the Magic Isle, The Magic of Oz
s: The magic of the Magic Isle enchants living entrants, including Trot and Cap'n Bill, causing roots to grow from their flesh into the ground. They cannot leave, shrink hour by hour and day by day, and eventually disappear; the Wizard seeks a way to overcome it.

l: danger threatening the beasts, The Magic of Oz
s: is_a threat to the liberty of the beasts The danger is presented as an attack by the Oz people, who allegedly intend to capture the beasts and enslave them. Ruggedo says he and Kiki came from the sky to warn the beasts and save them.

l: meeting of the beasts, The Magic of Oz
s: takes_place_in great clearing [for an occasion of great importance] The meeting takes place at sunrise in the Forest of Gugu's great clearing, with Gugu on a rock throne and the beasts gathered before him. The animals hear Ruggedo's speech, then give divided responses as Gugu asks them to consider the proposal carefully.

l: the monkeys, The Magic of Oz
s: The monkeys are forest-dwelling people and animals led by Rango the Gray Ape as chief of the forest monkey tribes. After fleeing giant soldiers, they return, recognize the giants as transformed friends and relatives, and gather. Twelve intelligent, good-tempered monkeys volunteer to accompany the Wizard of Oz to the Emerald City for Ozma's birthday. Temporarily three inches high and confined in a golden cage, they learn and perform the Wizard's tricks.

l: the forest, The Magic of Oz
s: The forest is a place ruled by Gugu, containing clearings, a hollow tree, monkeys, and a vast assemblage of animals. Kiki's transforming power scatters its inhabitants through the jungles. Ruggedo searches there, conspirators meet, and the Wizard hides. Trees imprison giant soldiers, and the animals later welcome the Wizard and Dorothy as trusted friends.

l: the black bag, The Magic of Oz
s: The Wizard’s black bag holds the magic tools needed to break transformations. Kiki Aru steals it, hides it hanging from a tree branch, and it is not found during the search. The Glass Cat later finds it, hides it under leaves, guides the Wizard to it, and enables its recovery.

l: Magic Tools, The Magic of Oz
s: Magic Tools inside the black bag can break enchantments when used properly. Kiki cannot identify their uses; when the Wizard regains them with the bag, they restore his confidence to rescue Trot and Cap'n Bill.

l: the enchantments, The Magic of Oz
s: Enchantments transform the Wizard of Oz into a Fox and Dorothy into a Lamb. Though the Wizard says they are easy to break with known methods and tools, Kiki's taking the black bag leaves the needed magic tools unavailable.

l: the search for the Black Bag, The Magic of Oz
s: is_undertaken_by the Wizard of Oz [after the bag is lost] The Wizard, Dorothy, the Cowardly Lion, the Hungry Tiger, and Gugu search the clearing and surrounding forest for the missing black bag. After the Glass Cat arrives, they decide to search for the Goose first, believing he may help them find the Magician and recover the bag.

l: the monkeys, The Magic of Oz
s: The monkeys, fifty in a clearing, gather in trees and are chosen for Ruggedo’s giant army; Kiki Aru transforms at least six into uniformed giant men carrying sharp swords.

l: the giant army, The Magic of Oz
s: A planned army of fifty monkeys transformed into uniformed, sword-carrying fifty-foot men begins with six giants created before the Wizard stops Kiki Aru; they remain standing in the forest.

l: the hollow tree, The Magic of Oz
s: The hollow tree provides hiding places for the Wizard of Oz in Fox form and later Kiki Aru when he whispers the Magic Word; through its opening, the Wizard hears the word and uses it for transformations.

l: the hickory-nut, The Magic of Oz
s: is_a transformed form of Kiki Aru [created by the Wizard] The hickory-nut is the form into which the Wizard transforms Kiki Aru. The Wizard picks it up and places it in his pocket as proof of what happened.

l: the walnut, The Magic of Oz
s: is_a transformed form of Ruggedo [created by the Wizard] The walnut is the form into which the Wizard transforms Ruggedo after correctly recalling the Magic Word. The Wizard picks up the walnut and places it in his pocket.

l: the Lonesome Duck, The Magic of Oz
s: The Lonesome Duck is the only duck in the Land of Oz, a uniquely colored, immortal bird living alone in its diamond palace a little way up the river, with food supplied by magic. It has no family, relations, friends, or occupation, dislikes everyone it meets, and is lonesome. Its simple magic serves its needs: when it cannot free Trot and Cap'n Bill, it performs an incantation to create each of them a comfortable, sturdy toadstool, then leaves.

is_caused_by lack of friends [and lack of family or occupation] Loneliness is described by the Lonesome Duck as existing for years without family, friends, or anything to do. The Duck claims that its disagreeable nature prevents it from making friends, while Trot argues that helping others could end its loneliness.

l: six giant soldiers, The Magic of Oz
s: Six giant soldiers, enchanted former monkeys, are made fifty-foot-tall men by Kiki Aru. Trapped among forest trees, they cannot move, raise their arms, or draw their sharp swords. They wear caps with red and yellow plumes until the Wizard of Oz breaks the enchantment and restores their natural monkey forms.

l: enchantment of the giant soldiers, The Magic of Oz
s: is_broken_by Wizard of Oz [restoring the soldiers to their natural forms] The enchantment turns six monkeys into enormous soldiers and leaves them helpless among the forest trees. The Wizard breaks it after Rango agrees to let twelve monkeys accompany him to the Emerald City.

l: golden cage, The Magic of Oz
s: is_made_from silver-and-gold dish [transformed by magic] The Wizard creates a golden cage with silver bars by using powder and fire in a silver-and-gold dish. The twelve selected monkeys are reduced to about three inches high and placed safely inside it.

l: the Magic Plant, The Magic of Oz
s: The Magic Plant, called the world's most beautiful by the Cowardly Lion, grows in a golden flower-pot on the Magic Isle. It rapidly produces hundreds of varied flowers: picked blooms remain perfect a long time, while unpicked ones soon disappear and are replaced.

l: the rescue of Trot and Cap'n Bill, The Magic of Oz
s: The rescue of Trot and Cap'n Bill begins when travelers reach the river opposite the Magic Isle. The Wizard promises help, sends the Glass Cat to reassure them, and prepares magic. His attempts fail because cutting or pulling their roots would cause severe pain, leaving them trapped and shrinking.

l: the cage of monkeys, The Magic of Oz
s: A cage made with golden wires holds the monkeys until the Hungry Tiger bends two bars; they escape, and Cap'n Bill later repairs the bars.

l: the twelve cake monkeys, The Magic of Oz
s: The twelve cake monkeys are small, long-tailed monkeys kept and carried in a cage. After the Glass Cat teases them by pulling their tails, and the Hungry Tiger bends two bars, they escape briefly to surround her and smear her with blue mud before returning to the cage. At Ozma's birthday party, they leap from a Surprise Cake, bow, dance, perform acrobatics, and play golden instruments.

l: the magic of the Wizard, The Magic of Oz
s: is_not_equal_to the magic of the Magic Isle [according to the Wizard's embarrassment] The Wizard's magic includes powders, liquids, magic words, explosive sparks, a magic axe, and silver pincers that can grow or shrink. Although he says he can break enchantments known to ordinary witches and magicians, his attempts do not free Trot and Cap'n Bill.

l: the island's enchantment trapping people, The Magic of Oz
s: The Magic Isle’s enchantment takes root in the feet of people and beasts made of meat, trapping them in the ground and making them shrink continuously. It roots Trot and Cap’n Bill when they walk on the island. Wood and glass, including wooden legs or soles and glass feet, are unaffected; leather shoes and wool stockings fail. The Wizard cannot break the magic or identify its creator.

l: Trot and Cap'n Bill's shrinking, The Magic of Oz
s: reduces half their natural sizes [at the time the Glass Cat reports it] Trot and Cap'n Bill shrink every minute while they are trapped on the Magic Isle. When the Glass Cat reports their condition, they are only about half their natural sizes, and Trot warns that soon nothing will be left of them.

l: the birthday banquet, The Magic of Oz
s: Ozma's birthday banquet gathers her closest friends, royal courtiers, and animal companions, with Ozma at the head table. She enters to an orchestra's march and cheering, enjoys the company, then watches twelve cake monkeys perform before it ends.

l: Trot and Cap'n Bill as bumblebees, The Magic of Oz
s: Transformed into bumblebees, Trot and Cap'n Bill fly from the Magic Isle to the riverbank, avoid the Hungry Tiger and Cowardly Lion, then speak to Dorothy.

l: Trot and Cap'n Bill's transformation into bumblebees, The Magic of Oz
s: The Wizard transforms Trot and Cap'n Bill into bumblebees to escape the Magic Isle, then reverses it, restoring their natural forms, sizes, and root-free feet.

l: Cap'n Bill's retrieval of the Magic Flower, The Magic of Oz
s: Cap'n Bill retrieves the Magic Flower from the Magic Isle by covering his good foot with wood, removing its golden pot, and carrying it safely to the riverbank.

l: the blue mud, The Magic of Oz
s: The blue mud is thick, slimy, dark blue, and paintlike when dry; from stream banks, monkeys smear it over the Glass Cat until it hardens on her body, eyes, and ears, then she washes it off.

l: the journey to the Emerald City, The Magic of Oz
s: is_slow slow journey [because the Wizard and Cap'n Bill travel on foot] The journey proceeds slowly because the Wizard and Cap'n Bill walk while the others carry the Magic Flower and the monkeys. The party camps beside a brook, resumes traveling the next day, and eventually arrives at the Royal Palace.

l: the monkeys' revenge on the Glass Cat, The Magic of Oz
s: is_a revenge [tit-for-tat for teasing] The monkeys take revenge after the Glass Cat repeatedly pulls their tails. They escape through the bent cage bars, seize the Glass Cat, cover her in blue mud, and return to the cage.

l: the Glass Cat's punishment, The Magic of Oz
s: is_a punishment [being covered in blue mud and publicly shamed] The Wizard considers the Glass Cat's blue-mud covering a punishment for teasing the monkeys and plans to let her be seen that way in the Emerald City. Dorothy cleans the mud from the cat's eyes and ears, but the Glass Cat must continue traveling with the mud on her body until she runs away to wash.

l: teasing the monkeys, The Magic of Oz
s: is_a tail-pulling [done by the Glass Cat] The Glass Cat teases the monkeys by slyly pulling their tails through the bars of their cage. Her teasing causes the monkeys to retaliate, and the Wizard says the punishment is deserved.

l: Professor H. M. Wogglebug, T.E., The Magic of Oz
s: Professor H. M. Wogglebug, T.E., Principal of the Royal Athletic College, invented the Tablets of Learning and Square-Meal Tablet. After forcing students to eat the tablets rather than ordinary food, the Senior Class threw him into a river; unable to swim, he was rescued after three days and appealed to Ozma for their punishment.

l: College of Athletic Arts, The Magic of Oz
s: is_a college [athletic] The College of Athletic Arts is located in the Munchkin Country, not far from the Emerald City. Its students use Tablets of Learning so they can devote their time to athletic exercises and sports.

l: Royal Athletic College, The Magic of Oz
s: Royal Athletic College, an athletic college in Munchkin Country near the Emerald City, is led by Professor H. M. Wogglebug; its Senior Class rebels over Square-Meal Tablets.

l: Tablets of Learning, The Magic of Oz
s: The Tablets of Learning, patented in Land of Oz by Professor Wogglebug, instantly teach mathematics, geography, spelling, handwriting, history, mechanics, home cooking, and agriculture, freeing Royal Athletic College students from book study for athletic exercises and sports.

l: Square-Meal Tablet, The Magic of Oz
s: The Square-Meal Tablet is a tiny tablet containing condensed soup, fried fish, roast, salad, and dessert, providing a full meal’s nourishment. Professor H. M. Wogglebug fed it to students instead of ordinary food, but they refused it for lack of meal taste.

l: Senior Class, The Magic of Oz
s: Senior Class of the Royal Athletic College refuses Square-Meal Tablets, seizes Professor H. M. Wogglebug, T.E., and throws him into a river; afterward, it is brought to the Emerald City for Ozma to decide punishment.

l: Betsy Bobbin, The Magic of Oz
s: Betsy Bobbin attends Ozma's birthday feast and is seated next to Aunt Em and before the Shaggy Man.

l: the Fountain of the Water of Oblivion, The Magic of Oz
s: The Fountain of the Water of Oblivion, on the palace grounds beside a marble bench, contains water causing forgetfulness; restored Kiki Aru and Ruggedo drink from it.

l: Ozma's birthday celebrations, The Magic of Oz
s: Ozma's birthday celebrations span the Land of Oz, beginning with bands preparing processions and continuing with decorations, games, plays, and festivities in four countries and Emerald City.

l: the Water of Oblivion, The Magic of Oz
s: causes_forgetting all previously known memories [after a person drinks it] The Water of Oblivion causes anyone who drinks it to forget everything previously known. Kiki Aru and Ruggedo drink it after their transformations and lose their identities, memories, and knowledge of magic.

l: the transformation of the magicians, The Magic of Oz
s: The Wizard transforms a hickory-nut into Kiki Aru and a walnut into Ruggedo, then makes them thirsty to drink the Water of Oblivion.

l: the Water of Oblivion's memory-erasing effect, The Magic of Oz
s: makes_harmless Ruggedo [after he drinks the Water of Oblivion] The memory-erasing effect removes a drinker's memories, identity, knowledge of magic, and understanding of personal history. It makes Kiki Aru innocent and makes Ruggedo forget his anger and plans to conquer Oz, leaving both harmless.
